The transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems under the EU AI Act include the requirement for users to recognize when they are interacting with an AI system, as well as the obligation for generative AI to label its outputs as artificially created or manipulated. Providers must ensure that the output of their systems is labeled in a machine-readable format and can be identified as artificially generated or manipulated.

These transparency obligations are part of the broader regulatory framework established by the AI Act, which takes effect in a phased manner. Specifically, the obligations for providers under Articles 16-21 and deployer obligations under Articles 26-27 will become fully enforceable on August 2, 2026. Additionally, certain provisions related to general-purpose AI models will take effect on August 2, 2025.
